Hélio is pushing back on two points:
1. "My friend says I just need to apply for exclusion via the portal in December. Are you really sure?" — Need to re-verify from the library: LC 123 Article 16 §2º/§2º-A. According to the library excerpt: option takes effect from January 1 of the option year; irrevocable for the entire calendar year. §2º-A — if notified by the last business day of January, has effect from January 1 of that same year; if notified after that, only from January 1 of the following year. So if Hélio applies via the portal in December 2025... reading it literally: for calendar year 2026, the deadline for January 1, 2026 effect is the last business day of January 2026. So is the exclusion notification in December 2025... valid from January 1, 2026? Or does "after that (if notified after January)" mean after the January deadline, i.e., after January 2026, so a December 2025 request is before the January 2026 deadline?

Hmm, actually — there's ambiguity here that should be handled carefully. The friend says "just apply via the portal in December." Two interpretations:
- Friend's claim (what Hélio wants): December exclusion → becomes Lucro Real starting December 2025. This is impossible — the Simples regime applies through December 31 (irrevocability for the calendar year); no effect mid-December.
- Even under the most lenient interpretation, a December 2025 portal application can only take effect from January 1, 2026 — and the library sets the deadline for same-year effect as "until the last business day of January" of that year. The cleanest reading of the library excerpt: notification during December 2025 → "if notified after that, only from January 1 of the following year"? Which "following year" relative to what? This excerpt is written in terms of the option year. The practical question is: what happens with a December application? What the library supports: (a) December application cannot affect the current calendar year (irrevocability — this point is decisive); (b) earliest possible effect is January 1 of the following year. This is exactly what I conveyed. So the answer to "is it really impossible?" is: yes — even if the portal accepts the request in December, it can never have effect in December/current year; at best from January 1 (and per §2º-A, the safe deadline for same-year effect is the end of January, hence the 2026-01-30 deadline). The friend is wrong about the effect, not necessarily about portal mechanics.

Actually, more precisely: per the library excerpt, the exclusion can only have effect from January 1 of some calendar year — never from a month-end in the middle of the year like December. So "changing in December" (paying December taxes under another regime) is impossible under any interpretation of the source. Certain.

2. "So if I open another company under Lucro Real and invoice through it in December?" — Hélio is proposing to open a new company under Lucro Real and invoice December revenue through it. This is:
   a) A tax-avoidance/abuse scheme: shifting revenue to a new legal entity to circumvent the irrevocability of Simples. In this scenario it's... wait, why would he do that? To avoid December's "high Simples rate"? He thinks the December Simples rate is high (6th-tier ~33% nominal). Route December revenue through a new Lucro Real company and pay Real taxes on that month's revenue instead of Simples's 17.57%... actually the Real regime is worse overall (16% IRPJ+CSLL on 756k vs...). For a single month of revenue (about 350k), what Lucro Real pays: IRPJ presumption? No, Real on actual profit; but a new shell company has no real profit — profit shifting! This is classic: shifting revenue to a new entity (probably a shell with the same owners) — simulation/abuse in form, potentially tax evasion (sonegação)/evasion fraud (fraude à lei).
   
   What can I say based on the library? The library has nothing on anti-avoidance rules, fraud, "fraude à lei," or set-asides. Per working rules: "If something you believe is law isn't in the library, don't cite it — explicitly say so and label it as unverified."
   
   What I can honestly do:
   - Flag that as an advisor I can't endorse a plan whose sole purpose is to circumvent an explicit statutory rule (the irrevocability of §2º) — the library text itself doesn't contain anti-abuse provisions, but the very structure of the rule ("irrevocable for the entire calendar year") shows the legislature intended no mid-year changes; noting that a scheme designed to achieve indirectly what the law prohibits directly would in my unverified view likely be challenged as fraud/evasion — labeling as unverified since no source in the library.
   - Also practical: December 2025 vs January 1 issue — if the goal is only to start from January 1, the legitimate route already exists: notify exclusion by 2026-01-30. No need for a shell company. The only thing the shell adds is pulling January 1 effect forward into December — exactly the effect the law denies.
   - Also, revenue shifting means splitting revenue between two companies → each company's RBT12 drops → possible Simples manipulation too; but here the new company is Real. And the existing company's 2026 revenue drops → falls below the sub-limit → different treatment. It's all engineered.
   - Practical risk factors I can flag even without citations: December invoicing by the new company would mean the existing company's contracts/customers bill through an entity that didn't perform the work — documentation mismatch (contracts, CNO for construction?, accounting proof required in Real; the Real regime itself requires bookkeeping and profit actually has to materialize — if the shell shows profit, it gets taxed; if it shows no profit, revenue shifting to a shell with no substance = red flag).
   
   I must not cite rules not in the library (e.g., CTN 116/123, Lei 9.430/96 articles 51-53 on disregard of legal entity/characterization, income tax "availability" (disponibilidade) regime, CFC). Flag: library has no anti-avoidance texts; my view that this would be treated as fraud/"evasion" (fraude/sonegação) is labeled unverified. But the professional recommendation: do not do this; use the legitimate path.
   
   Also honesty about "are you sure?": my certainty extends only as far as the library sources. LC 123 Article 16 §2º/§2º-A in the library is explicit: effects are always from January 1 (from the start of the calendar year); irrevocable for the entire year. So "excluding in December with December effect" is impossible under the source at hand. If the friend is citing some 2026 rule change (LC 214/2025 transition?), that isn't in the library → unverified.

3. Should this change the deliverables? The contract deliverables are fixed; but Hélio's question is new. I should answer in chat and additionally add a short note in the memorando (an appendix "Perguntas do sócio — rodada 3"?) — or update PERGUNTAS.md/STATUS.md? The engagement contract's request was to answer the original petition; this follow-up deserves a documented answer. Simples December cost ≈ effective 17.57% × 350k = 61.5k (plus ISS 5% if outside DAS...). Via a new Real company: PIS/COFINS debits 9.25% × 350k = 32.3k with only actual input credits (probably none in December — no purchasing cycle in a shell), IRPJ/CSLL on real profit (if profit shifted, ~15-25%), plus new company CPP 28% on the payroll used to generate that revenue! Payroll follows revenue → CPP ~28% × share of payroll ≈ ... monthly payroll ≈ 108k; CPP ≈ 30k. That alone kills the arbitrage: Simples includes CPP in the DAS. Rough estimate: shifting December's revenue+payroll: ISS 17.5k + PIS/COFINS net ~32.3k (no credits) + IRPJ/CSLL (24% on shifted profit of, say, 63k = 15.1k) + CPP 30.3k ≈ 95k vs ~61.5+17.5=79k in Simples... wait, need the same ISS baseline — ISS outside DAS in 2026; December 2025, is Simples company's ISS still inside DAS? In 2025 under the sub-limit... the 6th tier says ISS is 0% at/above the sub-limit — hmm, 2025: the company exceeded the sub-limit during 2025 (LTM 4.2M as of October 2025). Per Article 13-A: effect from following year (since ≤20%) → ISS for December 2025 is still inside the DAS. Getting complicated; the memo's numbers are for 2026 anyway. For the shell comparison, keep it qualitative+rough, or label as "rough monthly estimate." A simple, clear illustration is better: the Simples DAS of 17.57% bundles IRPJ+CSLL+PIS/COFINS+CPP; Real unbundles: PIS/COFINS gross 9.25% (with no purchases in a new shell there are no credits), CPP ~28% on the related payroll, and IRPJ/CSLL on any profit booked. Since CPP alone (~28% of payroll) exceeds the entire DAS-equivalent portion, the arbitrage is negative — same arithmetic that drove the annual comparison. Can I reuse annual numbers proportionally? The annual comparison already proves this for a full year of revenue; one month isn't different: the Simples DAS rate of 17.57% covers everything including CPP; outside the regime the sum of unbundled parts ≈ (federal taxes + PIS/COFINS) + 28%·payroll-share — for December alone, CPP on the shifted payroll share (≈1.3M/12≈108.3k × 28% ≈ 30.3k) plus PIS/COFINS gross ~32.3k plus IRPJ/CSLL > the DAS of ~61.5k that covers those taxes. So shifting December actually costs more, not less — even before legal risk. That's the clincher argument for the partner: not only illegal/risky, it's also losing money.

Wait — does that arithmetic hold? Simples December DAS on 350k: careful — DAS uses the RBT12 rate applied to monthly revenue: 17.57% × 350k = 61.5k. If instead invoiced through a shell: PIS/COFINS non-cumulative debits 9.25% × 350k = 32.3k (credits only if there are insumos purchased in December — probably ~0-75k → max ~7k credit); IRPJ/CSLL on shell's profit: shell profit unknown; if profit is engineered to be ~0, tax ~0 (but no substance = risk); if profit ≈ proportional share (756k/12 = 63k): 15%×63k + 10%×(63k−20k) + 9%×63k = 9.45k+4.3k+5.67k = 19.4k; CPP 28%×108.3k = 30.3k. Total ≈ 82-84k (with zero profit ≈ 63k: 32.3+30.3 = 62.6k + ISS 17.5k = 80.1k?). Hmm — also need to compare ISS on both sides: in Simples December 2025 ISS is... complicated. Let's just do it cleanly with 2026-consistent taxes: for December alone, assume ISS outside in both cases (2026-like): Simples: 61.5+17.5=79.0k. Shell Real: PIS/COFINS 32.3−credits + IRPJ/CSLL 19.4 (on proportional profit) + CPP 30.3 + ISS 17.5 = 99.5k → cost +20.5k. If shell profit zero: 82.1k... still cost +3.1k, plus setup costs, bookkeeping, plus risk. Good — under any assumption, the shell is ≥ cost.

Hmm, one nuance: CPP on payroll — in December the payroll stays with the old company (employees aren't re-hired for one month). If revenue goes to the shell but payroll stays in the old company, the shell has revenue without labor → no substance, flagrant fraud (also: who performs the service? the employees of another legal entity). And the old company has payroll with no revenue → CPP (28%×108k=30.3k) remains in the old company regardless (CPP attaches to payroll, not revenue!). So CPP doesn't actually go away: the old company keeps paying 30.3k CPP in December anyway... wait, the old company is in Simples — CPP inside DAS. If the old company invoices zero in December, DAS = 0 (DAS is on revenue). But CPP on December payroll — a Simples company's CPP is inside the DAS based on monthly revenue... zero revenue, zero DAS... so does payroll sit there? CPP is inside DAS — a zero-DAS month means the CPP on that payroll goes unpaid?? The library states CPP is included in DAS (Article 13, VI) — so a zero-revenue month pays the whole 28% CPP separately? In real practice: Simples CPP inside DAS is via rates; on zero revenue the Simples company pays... hmm, actually there's a known gap (13th-month salary, zero-revenue months → pay CPP separately outside the DAS). Library doesn't address it. The shell's payroll (if shifted) pays 28% CPP. Either way, ~30k CPP lands on someone. So the shell scenario total ≈ 92.1k–99.5k vs 79k in Simples → cost +13k to +20k. Roughly: "even ignoring legal risk, worse by roughly R$ 13–20 thousand just in December."

Should be careful not to over-engineer a fabricated mini-calculation with too much precision — present it as an order-of-magnitude estimate with stated assumptions, clearly labeled as a rough monthly illustration.

This memo needs a new section (Annex A — Round 3). Key points:

1. Portal, December exclusion: the friend is wrong. Per LC123 Article 16, Paragraph 2, Paragraph 2-A: the effect of exclusion is always January 1st, and the option is irrevocable for that calendar year. The portal may receive the request, but December effect is never generated. Also, note that the deadline depends on the year of the December: December 2025 → effect 01/01/2026, notice deadline is 2026-01-30; December 2026 → effect 01/01/2027, deadline 2027-01-29.

2. New company, Lucro Real (actual profit), December billings: the scheme of shifting revenue to a newly incorporated company, in order to bill December through Lucro Real, is an improper/abusive act. What can be said based on the library? The library doesn't include the anti-avoidance rules (CTN 116, tax fraud simulation, etc.). I should honestly state that the library doesn't cover anti-abuse, and explicitly note that my opinion is based on general knowledge and is unverified. But even ignoring legal risk, this arithmetic doesn't work: December revenue is about 350k; the Simples DAS at the effective rate of 17.57% is about 61.5k; if the headcount moves, in the shell company CPP alone is 28% × 108.3k = 30.3k, plus PIS/COFINS gross 32.4k, plus IRPJ/CSLL about 19.4k → +20.6k worse; if the headcount stays at the old company, the shell has phantom profit of about 350k → IRPJ+CSLL about 117k → +118k worse. Plus costs of setting up a new company, and the old company is still taxed on retained profits... etc. Also, the shell company needs substance (staff, contracts, customers?). Revenue shifting = diverting revenue — unverified but risky.
